problems.name: Overheating
problems.desc: Joints run hot under load, often with no visible sign until insulation or copper is damaged.

problems.name: Corrosion
problems.desc: Oxidised contact surfaces raise joint resistance, which raises temperature over time.

problems.name: Loose connections
problems.desc: Bolts loosen with vibration and thermal cycling, creating hot spots at the joint.

flow.name: Sensor straps
flow.sub: One per phase (R · Y · B), strapped on each critical joint

flow.name: Receiver
flow.sub: Collects readings from up to 60 sensors in the panel

flow.name: IoT gateway
flow.sub: ST-52 C on 4G, Ethernet or Wi-Fi, with local backup storage

flow.name: Cloud platform
flow.sub: I/O Sense stores data, checks limits and raises critical alerts

flow.name: Laptop / mobile
flow.sub: Live view, alerts, trends and reports for the maintenance team

hardware.name: Wireless bus-bar sensor strap
hardware.role: A battery-powered digital temperature sensor on a heat-proof strap, fitted directly on the bus-bar joint. Colour coded by phase.
specs: Non-conducting silicone strap, withstands up to 350 °C
1 min default (temperature sensed every 20 s; event record)
10 m / 35 ft (panel installation), 50 m / 165 ft line of sight
35 mm × 35 mm × 25 mm (390 mm strap length)
8 to 10 years, non-explosive lithium magnesium, replaceable
On a flat, clean surface of the bus bar

hardware.name: Receiver
hardware.role: Mounted in or near the panel. Listens to the sensor straps over RF and passes their readings to the gateway on Modbus.
specs: Spread spectrum technology, communicates with 60 sensors

hardware.name: ST-52 C IoT gateway
hardware.role: Reads every receiver on the Modbus line and sends the data to the cloud, keeping a local backup if the network drops.
specs: Up to 16–20 bus-bar controllers on Modbus RS-485

screens.name: Overview
screens.desc: How many joints are at normal, warning or critical temperature, and how many sensor batteries need attention. A live table shows incomer and outgoing temperatures for each phase of every feeder.

screens.name: Alerts & events
screens.desc: Every high-temperature and above-ambient event, with the device, start and stop time and how long it lasted. Exportable for maintenance records.

screens.name: Temperature trends
screens.desc: Each feeder’s R, Y and B phase temperatures over any date range, so a joint that is slowly heating up stands out before it fails.

screens.name: Reports
screens.desc: Scheduled reports of average phase temperatures per feeder, ready to share with the electrical and maintenance teams.
